title: attention-latency-spectrogram-investigation
summary: Exploratory notes for a spectrogram-style view of attention kernel latency across model sequence length, batch size, and concurrency. Comparing FlashAttention variant, paged attention implementation, and a fused-op path to identify regimes with p95/p99 degradation and root causes.
body:
Goal:
- Create an intuitive latency 'spectrogram' (sequence length vs batch size heatmap over percentiles) to spot transition regions where kernel choice causes p95/p99 spikes.
- Find reproducible microbenchmarks that expose worst-case tails and map them to kernel-level behaviors (register pressure, warp underutilization, page faults in paged KV, kernel launch jitter).

Environment:
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 80GB (PCIe), also spot checks on H100 and A10 for cross-checks.
- Driver/Cuda: NVIDIA driver 525.85, CUDA 12.2, cuBLAS 12, cuDNN 9.4.
- Runtime: rwinf-serving v1.14.2 (local dev build), attention libraries: flash-attn v2.1.3 (patched), paged-attn prototype commit 7b3c4f, fused-op microkernel set v0.9.
- Workload model: decoder-only LLM, 24 layers, hidden 2048, 32 heads. (Model is synthetic but uses same attention shapes).
- KV cache: enabled for all streaming tests.

Benchmark harness (how to reproduce):
- Use bench/attention_spectrogram.py (attached to GH PR) which iterates: sequence lengths = [32,64,128,256,512,1024,1536,2048,3072]; batch sizes = [1,2,4,8,16]; concurrency (parallel requests) = [1,4,8,16]. For each cell run 1200 warmup tokens + 2000 measured tokens, record per-token latency, and sample flame profiles every 500ms.
- Example command (container):
  docker run --gpus all -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \n    -v /mnt/models:/models rwinf/bench:2025-02 \n    python /bench/attention_spectrogram.py --model /models/synth-24l --kernels flash,paged,fused --out /tmp/spectrogram.csv

Key observations (high level):
1) Two distinct transition bands observed in spectrograms:
   - Band A: around seq=256-512 where Flash->Fused swap occurs; p95 increases by 30–60% when fused ops chosen for certain batch sizes.
   - Band B: around seq>=1024 where paged-attn p99 degrades sharply under concurrency >8, visible as vertical streaks.

2) FlashAttention path gives consistent median latency and good p95 for small batch sizes (1–4) up to seq=1024. Fused-op path reduces median for medium batches (8–16) at seq 128–512 but causes p99 spikes linked to register over-allocation.

3) Paged attention behaves well for single concurrency, but under multi-tenant or multi-concurrency situations it exhibits periodic large tail events. Flamegraphs show host-side serialization waiting on device-to-host page handling + kernel launch backoff.

Microprofiling evidence:
- nvprof / Nsight sampling at seq=512,batch=8,concurrency=8 (fused):
  - Kernel "fused_attn_k0" average runtime = 220us, but 0.5% of executions > 2.1ms.
  - SASS analysis: high register spill counts (estimated +48B local memory), causing memory load/store spikes.
- Nsight CPU side traces (paged-attn seq=2048, conc=16):
  - Intermittent CPU-side page fault handling (mmap/fallocate churn) and small sleeps (~3–5ms) in page manager thread correlating with p99 spikes.
- Device-side occupancy maps (flash vs fused):
  - Flash path: occupancy 78–90% across seq lengths up to 1024.
  - Fused: occupancy varies 40–85% depending on tile selection; worst cases at seq ~320 with odd tile mismatch.

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
1) Fused op kernel variants currently choose tile sizes by a heuristic that underestimates register usage for some head/hidden combos -> register spills -> slow paths and tail events.
2) Paged attention's async page manager has contention at high concurrency: many streams trigger page insert/eviction causing mutex contention and syscalls. Implementation encouraged paged-dedup path but it's not active.
3) Kernel launch jitter and scheduler backpressure when many small kernels are launched (batch=1..2, high concurrency) causes accumulated host-side serialization measurable as p99 tail.

Small experiments and sanity checks run so far:
- Patch fused kernel to prefer smaller per-thread register footprint (trade compute for more loads). Result: median increased ~5% for good cases but p99 reduced by ~60% for previously catastrophic cells (seq 256–512, batch 8).
- Disabled paged-attn async eviction: reduced p99 streaks but increased average memory usage; suggests eviction path contention was a main cause.
- Bundled kernel launches using CUDA streams aggregation (grouping sequences) decreased kernel launch overhead in small-batch high-concurrency regime; p95 improved by 20%.

Quant numbers (representative cells):
- seq=512, batch=8, conc=8:
  - Flash: p50=1.8ms, p95=2.5ms, p99=3.1ms
  - Fused (old heuristic): p50=1.6ms, p95=2.9ms, p99=12.2ms (heavy tail)
  - Fused (reduced-regs patch): p50=1.7ms, p95=2.6ms, p99=3.6ms
- seq=2048, batch=4, conc=16 (paged):
  - Paged: p50=6.4ms, p95=9.0ms, p99=25.3ms (spiky)
  - Paged (eviction sync off): p50=6.7ms, p95=8.7ms, p99=9.5ms

Artifacts collected and where to look:
- /tmp/spectrogram-raw.csv (full per-token samples)
- /tmp/nvprofiles/ - includes sampled SASS dumps for slow kernels
- GH PR linked above contains bench harness and fused kernel heuristic patch.

Immediate mitigations proposed:
- Ship fused kernel heuristic change as opt-in experiment behind a feature flag (baseline trade examined above).
- Add a paged-attn concurrency limiter and smarter batching for page manager (coalesce evictions, use lock-free queue).
- Implement a microbatch coalescer at the request router to reduce number of tiny kernel launches under heavy concurrency.

Longer-term directions and experiments:
- Build continuous spectrogram dashboards (per-model) in Console/Optimize so we can detect new transition bands when rolling new kernels or quant profiles. Heatmap should surface sequences where rollout will risk regression.
- Automatic kernel selector: use a small per-model sequence-distribution profiler (1000 requests) to choose kernel policy thresholds (flash vs fused vs paged) instead of static heuristics.
- Explore compiler-level register optimizations for fused path: trade code-gen for fewer spills, or split fused kernels into two-stage pipelines where register pressure is lower.
- Consider hybrid paged-attn fallback: if page manager queue depth > threshold, switch to flash variant for that request to avoid systemic tail events.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are there specific model shapes (head counts, dense vs sparse layers) that make fused-reg heuristic worse? Need cross-model sweep.
- On H100, do register pressure manifestations differ (different SM architecture)? Quick tests pending.
- Interaction with quantized kernels (int8/4bit): early tests show fused-reg patch behaves differently; need a dedicated quantized spectrogram.

Next actions (short list):
- (Aisha) push opt-in fused-reg heuristic flag with telemetry to record before/after cells by 2025-02-21.
- (Marcus) implement paged-attn eviction coalescer prototype and load test by 2025-02-25.
- (Lena) wire spectrogram CSV -> Console heatmap prototype and demo for Eng offsite 2025-03-03.
- (Diego) run H100 cross-checks and upload nvprofiles to /artifacts/h100/ by 2025-02-24.

Notes to self (raw log snippets):
- "hit p99 waterfall at 12:13PM, turned on regs-reduce patch, p99 collapsed — plausible signal"
- "flame snapshot 2025-02-16T12:13:48 shows big spikes in local memory stores inside fused_attn_k0"

Conclusion:
- The spectrogram view is proving effective to find banded transitions where kernel choice matters. Early fixes (reduced-reg fused kernel + paged eviction coalescer) look promising. Need to harden patches, expand to more shapes, and bake selection logic into runtime to avoid manual rollback cycles when deploying new kernels.

Attachments:
- bench harness (see GH PR), sample spectrogram CSV, nvprof traces, short screen recording of heatmap UI mock (on Slack thread).

If reviewers want, I can extract a minimal reproducible case that hits fused p99 > 10ms within a single docker command (sanity demo).
